cards.question: What causes death at release in crush syndrome?
cards.answer: Sudden release of potassium, acid, and myoglobin → hyperkalemic arrhythmia/cardiac arrest.

cards.question: Pre-release fluid for crush syndrome?
cards.answer: Normal saline ~1–1.5 L/h (adult) before extrication; avoid potassium-containing fluids.

cards.question: Drugs to prepare for crush hyperkalemia?
cards.answer: Calcium (chloride/gluconate), sodium bicarbonate, nebulized albuterol — per protocol.

cards.question: Mechanism of death in crowd crush?
Signs of traumatic asphyxia?
cards.answer: Facial/neck plethora, petechiae, subconjunctival hemorrhage, hypoxia.

cards.question: Crowd density danger threshold?
cards.answer: About 4–5 people per m² and rising, when individuals can't move independently.

cards.question: First hazard step at a rail incident?
cards.answer: Isolate power (overhead lines/third rail) before approaching.

cards.question: Why get the passenger manifest?
cards.answer: Transport incidents are closed — the manifest lets you account for every occupant.

cards.question: Floodwater danger depths?
cards.answer: ~6 inches (15 cm) of moving water can knock a person down; ~1 foot (30 cm) can float most cars.

cards.question: Priority in heat stroke?
cards.answer: Rapid cooling on scene (cold-water immersion best) before transport.

cards.question: Key protective steps for unaccompanied minors?
cards.answer: Identify, photograph, tag, keep in a supervised safe area, release only to verified guardians.

cards.question: Technology-dependent patients in disasters?
cards.answer: Home ventilators, O2 concentrators, dialysis, insulin — power/supply loss creates emergencies; plan early evacuation/power.
